content.text:
The Sea Keeps Its Own Counsel

I came down to the water at the hour
when the sky forgets which color it should wear,
and the sea, unhurried, folded its long shawl
of silver over stones that had waited there
since before the first word was spoken on this shore.

It does not answer questions. It only arrives,
then leaves, then arrives again, as if
returning were the whole of its philosophy.
Each wave writes a sentence in foam
and the sand erases it before I can read.

I have spent years trying to be that patient.
To lose a thing and let the tide take it,
to hold nothing so tightly it cannot move.
The gulls cry out their small complaints
and the sea listens without judgment.

Out past the breakwater, a freighter
slides across the horizon like a thought
someone meant to finish and didn't.
The sea keeps going. It always keeps going.
Salt dries white on my wrists.

Maybe that is the lesson: not to be vast,
but to return, and return, and return,
to wash the same stones with the same gentle insistence
until even the hardest things grow smooth
and learn, slowly, the shape of being touched.
